title: Aldehyde or Ketone? Structure and IUPAC Names
subject: Chemistry
objective: Methanal and propanone both have C=O, yet one is an aldehyde and one a ketone. Where the C=O sits decides it, and the names follow: -al for aldehydes, -one for ketones, plus the common names.

fill.q: In an aldehyde, the carbonyl carbon carries at least one ____ atom.
The IUPAC ending for aldehydes is ____.
The IUPAC ending for ketones is ____.
The common name of propanone is ____.

tf.q: In a ketone, the C=O group is at the end of the chain.
tf.explain: It is inside the chain, with carbon groups on both sides.

tf.q: The –CHO carbon of an aldehyde is always numbered C-1.
The smallest ketone has two carbon atoms.

ar.a: Ketones need a locant from five carbons on.
ar.r: The C=O can then sit at more than one position.

mcq.q: The IUPAC name of HCHO is:
Acetaldehyde is the common name of:

num.q: How many carbon atoms does the smallest ketone have?

short.q: State one structural difference between an aldehyde and a ketone.
short.solution: In an aldehyde the carbonyl carbon carries at least one H (C=O at the chain end); in a ketone it carries two carbon groups (C=O inside the chain).

match.explain: Each formula matches its IUPAC name.
